# Review — iliad-042 (7.92–180), first pass

Edits were made to `units.json` by script; `t` was never touched (checked: the units' `t`, joined, equal lines 92–180 of the archive; every `ln` is the line the unit starts on; `l` keeps the line division of `t`). `gloss.json` was not touched. Unit numbers below are by `ln`. Severity: HIGH = wrong English or a false statement a reader would be misled by and the validator or house rule would reject; MEDIUM = a grammatical label or house rendering that was wrong; LOW = loose wording, a wrong cross-reference, or a required addition.

Checked and found sound (no change): all 5 speeches (Menelaus 96–102, Agamemnon 109–119, Nestor 124–160, Nestor 171–174, the man who prays 179–180): “ on the first unit's `l` and `i`, ” on the last, `mark` on the first unit of each; 7.92 follows Hector's speech, which iliad-041's last unit closes with ”. `p` on the five ¶ units (92, 103, 120, 161, 175). Whole-unit repeats (7.92, 7.132 first line, 7.177) keep the published English. 7.119 and 7.174 are identical in `l` and `i`. Cross-references checked against the edition: 2.235, 2.255, 2.258, 2.371, 2.401, 2.404, 2.651, 2.736, 3.95, 3.318, 3.364, 4.170, 4.319, 4.389, 5.285, 5.810, 6.62, 6.130, 6.325, 7.8–10, 7.25, 7.75, 7.81, 1.266, and Odyssey 9.214, 12.98, 21.107, 22.114 are all true (exceptions below).

## Findings considered and refused

- **7.98 εἶσιν (flagged doubt).** The label is true: εἶσιν is the third singular of εἶμι ‘go’. The note says the form “can be read as an indicative or as an old subjunctive; the sense is the same”, which is a hedge, not a false label, and `l`/`i` “goes” fit either. Left.
- **7.100 ἀκήριοι.** “spiritless”, ἀ- + κῆρ, matches conventions row 5.812 (“spiritless”, not “uninjured”) and the note already says the formation is uncertain and sets it against Odyssey 12.98. Left.
- **7.156 παρήορος (flagged doubt).** The note says the sense is unknown, that the word is built on παρά and the root of ἀείρω, and that elsewhere it is a horse harnessed beside the others (16.152); all true, and “stretched out” is declared a guess. Left.
- **7.146 ἐξενάριξε “stripped off”.** The house `l` for ἐξεναρίζω is “despoiled” (iliad-026, -028, -033, -036, -039) and the drafter's `l` departs from it. Refused as a change because those rows all take a person as object; with τεύχεα as object “despoiled the armour” is not English, and the departure is argued in new-renderings and the note. Flagged for the caller: if the validator or a later reviewer insists on “despoiled”, the line would be “and the armour he despoiled, …”.
- **7.118 ἀσπασίως “gladly” / “with joy”.** Matches Odyssey conventions 8.450 and 10.131 exactly. Left.
- **7.118 γόνυ κάμψειν.** Note rightly says the Greek has only “bend the knee”; left.
- **7.171 `i` “for whoever is allotted it”.** Slightly stiff, but it carries ὅς κε λάχῃσιν without adding anything; left.
- **7.97 ὕπερθε “opens the second clause”.** The clause opens with αὐτάρ and ὕπερθε follows at the line end; the note's wording is loose, not false. Left.
- **7.127 ἐρέων “from ἐρέω, a form of the same verb”.** Label is true (ἐρέω/ἐρέομαι ‘ask’ beside εἴρομαι); the other reading (future of ἐρέω ‘say’) does not suit the sense. Only the construction was changed (above).
- **7.127 `l` “asking of all the Argives the lineage and the birth”.** Kept in Greek order; the note now says how it is meant.
- **7.151 `i` “to face him”.** Supplies an object the Greek leaves out; the note says the Greek leaves it unsaid and new-renderings records the choice. Left.
- **7.136 καλλίζωνοι, ἰσόθεος φώς, κορυθαίολος, δῖος, εὐρὺ κρείων, Γερήνιος ἱππότα Νέστωρ, ἱππηλάτα, ἐγχεσίμωροι, ὠκυρόῳ, χάλκεος Ἄρης, μῶλον Ἄρηος, προκαλίζετο, προφρονέως, εὖχος, ἀνδρειφόντης.** All checked against the tables; consistent.

## For the caller

`new-renderings.md` was not touched (not in scope) and now disagrees with `units.json` in three rows: ἀναΐξαντες ἕλον (row says “leaping up … seized” / “leapt up and seized”, and lists “sprang” among the words avoided; units now have “having sprung up … seized” / “sprang up and seized”), ἔρριγ’ ἀντιβολῆσαι (row says “shrinks to meet” / “shrinks from meeting”; units now have “shudders to meet” / “shudders to meet him”, ῥιγέω keeping “shudder”), and ἐπίκλησιν κορυνήτην … κίκλησκον (row says the -σκ- iterative is shown by “used to”; it is not an iterative there). Second pass should also read `gloss.json` against the line, in particular the parses of μέμαθ’ (2nd plural μέματε), ὦρτο (augmented), ἐρέων, κίκλησκον (not iterative) and ὅθ’ (ὅθι).

# Pass 2

Read `gloss.json` (117 novel entries, 11 `__broaden__` entries) against the lines, `units.json` once more in full, and `new-renderings.md`. `units.json` was not changed in this pass (`t` untouched in both passes). `gloss.json` was edited in place by script; `new-renderings.md` was edited (three rows agreed to `units.json`, and one false clause removed). Checked after editing: every novel key of `novel-forms.json` has an entry and there is no extra key; every novel entry is under 230 characters (longest 189), has no line number, no “here”/“line”, and no quote mark other than ’; every `__broaden__` entry still begins with the whole old entry from `known-forms.json`, and only the added reading was altered.

## Parses the caller asked about

- **μέμαθ’ (7.159):** entry said “μέμαα … perf. 2 pl. … elided”, which agrees on person but not on lemma or on the aspiration the unit note gives. Now “μέμονα (μέμαα) … perf. 2 pl. μέματε with present sense, elided, the τ aspirated to θ before a rough breathing”; it agrees with the note (μέματε, ‘you’, matching ὑμέων). Kept: `l` ‘they’ for οἳ is the relative subject of the 2nd-plural verb, as the note says.
- **ὦρτο (7.162):** not a novel form; the known entry (“ὄρνυμι … aor. 3 sg. ὦρτο, root aorist: ‘rushed, started up’”) covers ‘rose’ and makes no claim of absent augment. Sound, no broadening needed (the form is ἐ-ὄρτο, augmented).
- **ἐρέων (7.128):** parse (pres. part., uncontracted, + acc. of the thing γενεήν τε τόκον τε) agrees with the corrected note. The entry did not name an Attic equivalent as the glosser rule requires; added “(= Attic ἐρωτῶν)”.
- **κίκλησκον (7.139):** parse was right (impf. 3 pl. of κικλήσκω, unaugmented) but the entry was silent on -σκ-; it now says the -σκ- is part of the present stem, not an iterative suffix, which agrees with the note.
- **ὅθ’ (7.143):** the known entry already has ὅθι first and ὅτε second; the note and the line (ὅθι ‘where’) agree. No change.

## Re-read of `units.json`: nothing further to change

Every unit re-read against the Greek and `l`/`i`: no new HIGH or MEDIUM finding; pass 1’s changes hold. Points looked at and left:

- **7.159 `l` “not even they are readily eager”.** The Greek verb is 2nd plural (μέματε) with οἳ as relative subject; `l` renders οἳ ‘they’ and the note says so. Refused as a change: `l` is the word-for-word layer, and `i` has ‘those of you’.
- **7.113 “Ἀχιλεύς has a single λ for the metre”.** True of the printed spelling (the short syllable needs one λ); left.
- **7.172 “here his life”.** Notes may point at their own line; left.
- **7.136–7.139 `l` ends on a comma with no main verb, 7.142 `l` “where then not the club for him destruction / warded off”.** Literal, as `l` is; `i` is clean. Left.
- **7.151 ἐδείδισαν “a past form of δείδω”.** Loose but true (the known entry gives aor. 3 pl. in -σαν); left.
- **7.97 εἶσιν:** the known entry says “pres. 3 sg.”, the note allows an old subjunctive; the hedge is already refused in pass 1.
- **Known forms checked for coverage** against the readings in this part (ὅθ’, ὅτ’, ὦρτο, ᾧ, ὅς, ὅ, οἳ, οἵ, οἱ, τῷ, τοῦ, τοῖσι, ἐκ/ἔκ/ἐν in tmesis, ἀνῆκε, ἔτλη, ἔνι, ἂν, κε/κεν (potential optative at 125, 130, 158 is in κε/κεν), αὐτός/αὐτὸς, μὴ with εἰ and the aorist, δῖος/δίῳ, ἕκαστοι, ἐγένοντο): all covered; no further `__broaden__` entry needed.
